anti_overlap: Do not evaluate genre fidelity to DF/Qud, simulation-regime naming (settle vs. deferred-cascade), or chronicle delivery UX — that belongs to fd-worldgen-history-simulation-depth.
Do not evaluate narrative texture, the simulate-vs-author line, or lore/flavor-text ownership — that belongs to fd-procgen-narrative-simulate-author.
Stay on Souls-model scope, determinism/replay semantics, regeneration durability, and the storage dimension of the cost curve.
decision_lens: In an event-sourced system, every 'is X a Soul' question is a determinism and storage-growth commitment, not a modeling preference — it decides what gets replayed, what gets versioned, and what a regeneration event is allowed to discard. A goal that leaves Soul-scope, determinism semantics, and log-growth unaddressed cannot be tested by cargo test in any way that actually verifies the properties DONE WHEN claims.
focus: Event-sourced simulation architecture for the Souls model — determinism boundaries across regenerated strata, replay/cascade-invalidation semantics, and the storage/log-growth dimension of the cost curve.
name: fd-eventsourcing-strata-regen-contract
persona: Apply the perspective of a distributed-systems and event-sourcing architect experienced in CQRS-style aggregate replay, deterministic simulation engines, and designing rebuild/regeneration contracts for layered systems where upper strata derive from and must survive changes to lower-stratum state.
review_areas: GATE poses 'are celestial bodies Souls... or plain data' as open, but DONE WHEN's Reynolds-ruins bullet already commits to an answer in effect — 'evidenced by the event log itself' for a fallen civ's ruins at 'a real location' implies the location-bearing entity (the planet/site) must itself carry or be addressable through an event log, which is a Souls-model commitment GATE claims is still undecided. The goal is internally inconsistent about how settled this fork already is.

The determinism claim in DONE WHEN ('generates deterministically from the world seed') is unqualified for a stratified, regenerable system: determinism must be scoped per-stratum-boundary (same seed + same lower strata ⇒ bit-identical upper strata? or same seed alone, tolerating re-divergence above any regenerated stratum?). Without this, 'cargo test --workspace green' cannot encode a meaningful determinism test — a test asserting seed-in/history-out equality would be either untestable (if regeneration is expected to diverge) or wrong (if it isn't).

DONE WHEN's cost curve is scoped as 'systems × civs × members × centuries' — a compute/CPU-shaped formula — but for an event-sourced model the dominant scaling wall is typically event-log volume and replay time as history accumulates, not raw compute per tick. Neither GATE nor DONE WHEN asks about storage growth or replay cost, so the probe could report a clean compute-cost curve while silently building an unreplayable, unbounded event log — the 'affordability envelope' referenced is not tied to a specific resource dimension.

GATE's 'worlds disposable until played' regeneration stance is not reconciled with the Reynolds-ruins DONE WHEN requirement: if a fallen civilization's ruins are generated but the player never visits before a lower stratum regenerates, the goal never specifies whether that civ's coordinates/event log survive the regeneration or are discarded as 'unplayed.' This is exactly the kind of stratum-boundary durability question event-sourced layered systems get wrong by default, in the direction of silently losing history.

Beads filed for 'strata deliberately stubbed' (DONE WHEN) have no requirement that the stub interfaces be schema-versioned; in an event-sourced model, later deepening a stubbed stratum (e.g., giving species stubs real Dixon-grade evolution) means either replaying old event logs against a new schema or breaking every already-generated world — OUTCOME's 'interfaces designed for later deepening' language doesn't commit to which, and this is the standard failure mode of unversioned event schemas in long-lived event-sourced systems.

severity_examples.condition: If the brainstorm mk holds treats 'are celestial bodies Souls' as genuinely open per the GATE wording, but engineering has already built the Reynolds-ruins path assuming planets carry event logs (per DONE WHEN's literal requirement), the brainstorm ruling could contradict already-built architecture, forcing a rework the goal's sequencing ('rulings... before implementation starts') was supposed to prevent.
severity_examples.scenario: Souls-scope answered implicitly, then re-litigated in the brainstorm

severity_examples.condition: If cargo test encodes seed-to-full-history determinism without the goal having scoped what determinism means across a regenerated stratum, the test either fails during legitimate future-stratum deepening (false positive) or passes while masking real nondeterminism introduced by concurrent derivation (false negative).
severity_examples.scenario: determinism test asserts the wrong invariant

severity_examples.condition: If the probe reports systems×civs×members×centuries against wall-clock time only, a slice-one run could look affordable while the underlying event store grows unboundedly per century simulated, and the next engine bottleneck (storage, not compute) goes unmeasured — directly contradicting the goal's own 'measured rather than guessed' claim.
severity_examples.scenario: cost curve blind to log growth

success_hints: Check whether the goal's Reynolds-ruins DONE WHEN bullet is consistent with GATE treating celestial-bodies-as-Souls as still open, and flag the inconsistency if the two disagree.
Look for an explicit definition of determinism scoped to stratum-regeneration boundaries, not just 'generates deterministically from the seed'.
Verify the cost-curve formula in DONE WHEN accounts for event-log/storage growth, not only compute across systems×civs×members×centuries.
Check whether 'worlds disposable until played' is reconciled with the durability requirement implied by queryable ruins.
Flag whether stubbed-stratum interfaces are required to be schema-versioned so later deepening doesn't break already-generated event logs.
task_context: Domain framing: this review applies event-sourcing and layered-system architecture expertise — CQRS-style aggregate replay, determinism boundaries, and regeneration/rebuild contracts — to a draft goal built on an event-sourced 'Souls' entity model. Stress-test this draft goal (stratified worldgen at DF/Qud depth for Mind State, slice one on the palettice engine) before ratification: find missing forks, scope traps, wrong assumptions, and anything the GATE/DONE WHEN/OUT structure gets wrong.
